title: Drum breaks, Mack Murray's traps and wood blocks
summary: Old drummers kept the beat; Mack Murray dropped chains and blew whistles in breaks, others used bottles and cowbells, and Barbarin wants a good wood block.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Did the drummers take many breaks in the old days? No.
Drummer's always kept the beat. It wasn't nothing.
They wouldn't even take a two-bar break?

Well, yeah. Well, a two-bar break. Yeah. I mean, you know. Mack Murray took a lot of two-bar breaks, but I can recall. Mack Murray used to drop the chain, blew the whistles, racket. He had a racket with a break on a racket. He had a lot of doodads. I mean, you see, he was a Mack Murray. He was a great drummer.
He had a big set then, with all his traps.
Yeah, he had a great big bass drum, I remember that. And he had a little bit of banjo, head snare drum. Like a banjo, made like a banjo. Sharp, too. It was good. He was a good drummer. Good beat.
Do you remember any other traps he had, other than the chain and the whistles?

No, I can't recall. Oh, yeah, I'd call a little late on in years Joe Renier, Kid Renier's brother. He played a tune on it. He had some wine bottles. He had some coca-cola bottles. He had jumbo bottles. All kind of bottles. And he'd play a tune, play a waltz on those bottles. That's right. I'm not kidding.
Ever see tuned cowbells? Huh? You ever see tuned cowbells? Oh, yeah, there's four of them, I mean, yeah.
I've seen them. Many people here use them?
No, no.
A whole lot of fellas didn't use that, though. How many cowbells would they have in those?
Four.
Four. They would have four. The big one, the next size, the next size, the next size, the small one, you know.
Four on a line, you know.
Two in the back, two in the front, you know. And that dates way back then, huh?
Oh, yeah, that dates way back.
Oh, yeah, that dates way back. Oh, yeah, that dates way back. Mm-hmm.
Wood blocks? Yeah, wood blocks.

Those days they had some good wood blocks. I can't find me a good wood block. I would like to run into one of them. There's a little small wood block and it's black, like, and good material, I mean, there's a good material, I mean. You can't run into those. I've been trying to find one because I like to use it, I mean.
What about those tempo blocks? You know what I mean?
Oh, no, I had those. I don't like that. I mean, no. I gave them away.
When did that come in? Oh, let's see.

Well, I can recall that came around 20, uh, 24, 25, I remember. I had a set around that time, yeah. I might have been a little before that, you know, but I mean, that's the time I had a set. That's about as far as I can remember having a set, you know. Do you remember any particular tunes that Mike Murray would take breaks in? No, I can't, uh, it's a tune that, uh, I can't recall his tune, uh, he had a, a wagon, a wagon chains. Uh-huh. And he'd hold them in the air and he'd, and he'd drop the chains to make a two-bar break. Right on time. I don't know what tune it was. I mean, I had to catch, catch one of the old timers, I mean, uh, you know, guys that, around that time, you know, to find out what tune that was, you know. But what has happened to a cymbal playing through the years? Uh-huh.
